title: The full test suite never fails on unchanged code when the Mac is busy
goal: Some checks in the test suite fail now and then in a full run and pass on their own, so a runner or a release cannot trust a red run and has to run the whole suite again. One is a timing check judged against a flat number of milliseconds; three are video checks (a size estimate, a cut export, a moving title background). Each one either reads something the rest of the suite changes, or shows a real problem under load: find out which and fix it.
notes:
Reproduced 2026-11-02 in asking-for-a-sheet-of-components-gives-a-clean-t, tree with only Agent component planner changes:
  $ Scripts/test.sh
  ✘ Test dragTheWidth() recorded an issue at ShapeBorderRenderTests.swift:262:13: Expectation failed: (median → 52.961916) < (48 → 48.0)
  ✘ Test dragTheWidth() failed after 181.377 seconds with 1 issue.
  ✘ Test run with 1331 tests in 207 suites failed after 219.950 seconds with 1 issue.
Same tree:
  $ Scripts/test.sh --filter ShapeBorderRenderTests  ->  ✔ dragTheWidth() passed after 0.351 seconds; 8 tests passed
  $ Scripts/test.sh  ->  all five groups passed (15,197 tests)
The check is `if MachineSpeed.isGating { #expect(median < 48) }` in the suite "A Width drag on a drawn package stays inside a frame" (Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/ShapeBorderRenderTests.swift:201), which runs in the rest group beside three other swift test processes, not with the stopwatch suites. CLAUDE.md: a speed budget goes in a ...PerfTests suite and is judged against a ruler taken beside it, never a flat millisecond count.

Folded in 2026-11-03 from the-full-test-run-never-fails-on-a-video-check-t:
Seen while measuring the-full-test-run-never-fails-on-a-speed-budget, 2026-10-30, in about 25 full Scripts/test.sh runs on this Mac (16 cores, go loop idle):
- BusyVideoSizeTests.swift:251 (A long recording that is quiet and then busy is weighed from stretches of it): near(landed 2102302, weighed 1597442) failed, once.
- BusyVideoSizeTests.swift:148 (Where the budget cannot hold, what the sheet weighs is what lands, speed 900): near(landed 1712276, weighed 1339509) failed, once.
- VideoCutExportTests.swift:35 (Exporting a recording with the middle dropped writes only what is left): Caught error .readerGaveUp("no picture came out of the recording for 30 seconds"), once.
Both BusyVideoSizeTests are in the .serialized run (Scripts/test.sh side run). Command: Scripts/test.sh with no arguments; output lines above are verbatim from those runs. Neither is a speed budget, so they were left out of the speed-budget task.
acceptance: The width-drag timing is judged against a ruler taken beside it (MachineSpeed / PerfClock) or moved into a PerfTests suite that runs with nothing beside it
Scripts/test.sh passes three runs in a row with the probe building beside it, on unchanged code
The busy-video size estimate and the cut export that waits 30 s for its recording are each reproduced or explained: what about a busy Mac makes the weighed size miss, and what holds the reader

The Aurora and Behind Glass check (TitleBackgroundsRenderTests: playback, scrubbing and export draw the same frames) passes 20 full Scripts/test.sh runs in a row, or its difference is shown to be GPU rounding with numbers and bounded to 1 level per pixel
A real defect in the app found on the way (an estimate that is wrong under load, a reader that stalls) is fixed, not loosened in the test
None of these checks fails in ten full Scripts/test.sh runs in a row on this Mac
